written_by_hand: The archive-level record of the rolling-arm (R) TabPFN grid run on the Apple node: the node's console log for this stretch, the job list the runner walked and its cumulative tally, copied unchanged from the result archive, and the facts that belong to the archive rather than to one job. The eighteen job directories listed under jobs hold the rows and a manifest each.
host: Apple M4 Pro laptop, 24 GB unified memory, macOS 26.6.2, Python 3.12.14; the machine of experiments/2026-09-04-m4pro-tabpfn-timing and experiments/2026-09-11-lc-grid-e-tabpfn-m4pro
gpu: Apple Silicon GPU (arm64), Metal via torch 2.14.0 MPS, memory shared with the system

job_archive.provenance: Both copies equal the files in scripts/ at c44985a; score_context.py is unchanged since fd5eadf and node_jobs.py since 1b13842; both equal the copies in the E grid's and the TabICL grid's job archives.

result_archive.name: outoftime-result-grid-r-tabpfn.tar.gz
result_archive.contents: eighteen output directories, score.log, jobs.json, jobs-done.json; kept in Downloads and under data/derived/node/ with a .sha256 sidecar

process.one_process_no_resume: node_jobs.py walked the eighteen R jobs of jobs.json in order in one call of run.sh, one score_context.py call per job into its own output directory, tallying each finished job in jobs-done.json; the eighteen finish times are in the order of the job list, the first at 2026-09-12T18:04:23Z and the last at 2026-09-15T01:26:52Z, every gap between one job's finish and the next job's start is under a minute in either direction, and no job was skipped or resumed. jobs-done.json is the node's tally file and is kept across calls of run.sh: by the end it holds 38 entries, the E grid's eighteen (one earlier call, finishing 2026-09-07 to 09), the two 2015H1-E folds entries (another call, 2026-09-12), and these eighteen, each tallied once. The R call started 3,479 s after the folds call finished.
process.console_log: score.log here is the node's whole console output, appended to across the E grid, the folds job and the R grid: lines 1 to 838 are the E grid's eighteen jobs, 839 to 876 the 2015H1-E folds job, and 877 to 1704 the eighteen R jobs this index describes, in order; the 877-to-1704 slice is what each R job directory keeps as its own score.log. The E-grid prefix (lines 1 to 838) is byte-identical to experiments/2026-09-11-lc-grid-e-tabpfn-m4pro/score.log. Read in full: no home path, no account name, no token; the checkpoint was on the machine and nothing was downloaded.
process.incidents: None flagged for the R stretch: no cell in the eighteen R jobs runs more than 1.054x its cohort-and-context median, unlike the lid and sleep episodes recorded against three of the E grid's jobs. That is a bookkeeping check against the R cells themselves, not a performance measurement; see timing below.
process.timing: The 18 R jobs sum to 208,284.8 s of wall, 57.9 h, over the 2026-09-12T18:04:23Z to 2026-09-15T01:26:52Z stretch, and none of it is a measurement in the sense of experiments/2026-09-04-m4pro-tabpfn-timing: the machine's other use across that stretch is not independently checked, only that no cell here is an outlier against its own kind. A 50,000-row-context cohort cell (20,000 rows) ran 311 to 337 s, close to the 319.5 s idle-machine figure that manifest recorded; a 31,016-row-context cohort cell, scored only on build 2013H1-R, ran 140 to 141 s and is not compared to that figure, since the context size differs.

checks_over_all_eighteen.bundle_hashes: node.json's bundle hashes equal bundle.json of the build's bundle directory, all eighteen
checks_over_all_eighteen.parts: part files equal node.json cell records in number (60, 54, 48, 42, 36, 30, 24, 18, 12 for each of the two passes on the nine builds, largest build first); concatenated parts equal scores.parquet and reference.parquet, all eighteen
checks_over_all_eighteen.rows: every scored (cohort, row), its outcome and age match the gbm rows of the build's score run; every reference row and outcome match the gbm-50k reference of the same context seed; zero mismatches, no missing probability; the cohorts scored are the build's test cohorts; all eighteen
checks_over_all_eighteen.parameters: softmax_temperature 0.9 on the nine tabpfn jobs and 1.0 on the nine tabpfn-t1 jobs, balance_probabilities false, categorical_features_indices [6, 13, 19], ignore_pretraining_limits true, n_estimators auto, random_state 0, context rows equal to min(train_rows, 50000) on every model of every node.json
checks_over_all_eighteen.repeats: the first cohort of every context seed scored twice from a fresh fit: largest disagreement 0.0, no row differs, all 54 repeats

against_earlier_contexts_on_this_machine.reading: No R context draw is bit-identical to any context this machine has already scored (the nine E bundles, the 2015H1-E folds and folds-2to5): the largest row overlap between an R context and any earlier one ranges from 30,678 of 31,016 rows (2013H1-R against 2013H1-E, which share most of the same short pool) down to 2,265 of 50,000 (2017H1-R against 2017H1-E, whose pools barely overlap), and no pair is identical. This is expected: the R arm draws from a rolling four-quarter pool that the E arm's expanding pool does not reproduce, so unlike the within-machine repeat check above, there is no bit-identity cross-check for the R grid against anything scored before it — only the row-identity check against each build's own gbm score run, which is exact.

checks_over_all_eighteen.environment: Python 3.12.14, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, torch 2.14.0 on mps, tabpfn 8.5.0, checkpoint d0d865d5...3988, tabicl 2.1.1 present and unused, peak 2.478 to 3.652 GB of unified memory across the eighteen node.json files, and every field the E grid's environment_table carries is equal between the two grids except context_rows (31,016 or 50,000 here against a flat 50,000 on the E grid), the nearest and peak_gpu_gb_* fields that follow from that, and seeds, which differs only because the E-side comparison set includes the single-seed 2026-09-06 probe manifest alongside the eighteen grid jobs.

not_in_this_run: TabICL, scored on the hosted notebook (experiments/2026-09-13-lc-grid-r-tabicl-colab-t4 and the nine directories it indexes). The per-build poolings with these directories added, and the H4 reading against arm E, are written against.
